title: Arbitrary ring-sheaf coefficient change preserves the clopen proper/open mate
statement:
Let $k:U\hookrightarrow V$ and $i:W\hookrightarrow Z$ be quasi-compact open immersions of schemes, and let $r:U\to W$ and $p:V\to Z$ be proper, with $pk=ir$ [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Use small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Choose either their ordinary sites or their vertical sequence sites, whose sheaves are inverse sequences of sheaves, with topology generated by the coverings at each fixed index [lem-weil-pbc-diagram-site-realization, lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]. On the chosen site of $Z$ let $a:A_Z\to B_Z$ be any map of sheaves of commutative rings; in the sequence case this is a compatible map of inverse ring systems. On every other scheme in the square and its fibre products use inverse images of these rings and ring maps. Let $D(A_T)$ and $D(B_T)$ be the ordinary unbounded derived categories of module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and put $S_T=B_T\otimes^L_{A_T}-$ [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. Use the canonical ringed derived adjunctions $v_D^*\dashv Rv_{*,D}$ for $D=A,B$, with unit $\eta_{v,D}$ and counit $\varepsilon_{v,D}$ [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact]. Write $\lambda_v:v_B^*S_{\mathrm{target}(v)}\xrightarrow{\sim}S_{\mathrm{source}(v)}v_A^*$ for canonical balanced pullback. Define the coefficient map $\chi_v:S_{\mathrm{target}(v)}Rv_{*,A}\to Rv_{*,B}S_{\mathrm{source}(v)}$ to be the $v_B^*\dashv Rv_{*,B}$-adjunct of $S_{\mathrm{source}(v)}(\varepsilon_{v,A})\lambda_v$. For an open $j$, let $\delta_j:Sj_{!,A}\xrightarrow{\sim}j_{!,B}S$ be the open-unit-normalized coefficient comparison [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization].

Put $V_W=V\times_ZW$, with projections $b:V_W\to V$, $q:V_W\to W$, and clopen immersion $s=(k,r):U\to V_W$ [def-pc-fibre-product, lem-cbc-strict-tower-proper-open-calculus]. For $D=A,B$ let $\pi_s^D:N\to s_{!,D}s_D^*N$ be identity on $s(U)$ and zero on its complementary open. Let $\beta_D:p_D^*i_{!,D}\xrightarrow{\sim}b_{!,D}q_D^*$ be the open-unit-normalized open base-change comparison, and set
$$t_D:p_D^*i_{!,D}\xrightarrow{\beta_D}b_{!,D}q_D^*\xrightarrow{b_{!,D}\pi_s^Dq_D^*}b_{!,D}s_{!,D}s_D^*q_D^*\xrightarrow{\sim}k_{!,D}r_D^*.$$
The last arrow uses the canonical open and pullback compositors. Define its proper mate by the actual formula
$$\Gamma_D=Rp_{*,D}(k_{!,D}\varepsilon_{r,D})\circ Rp_{*,D}(t_DRr_{*,D})\circ\eta_{p,D}i_{!,D}Rr_{*,D}:i_{!,D}Rr_{*,D}\longrightarrow Rp_{*,D}k_{!,D}.$$
Then for every $M\in D(A_U)$ there is an equality in $D(B_Z)$,
$$Rp_{*,B}(\delta_{k,M})\circ\chi_{p,k_{!,A}M}\circ S_Z(\Gamma_{A,M})
=\Gamma_{B,S_UM}\circ i_{!,B}(\chi_{r,M})\circ\delta_{i,Rr_{*,A}M}.$$
The equality is natural in $M$. It holds on the whole derived categories of systems before evaluation or total limit in the sequence case. Neither flatness of $a$, boundedness, constructibility, invertibility of any $\chi$ or $\Gamma$, nor cartesianness of the scheme square is assumed.

proof.text: Use ringedRefinementCore to obtain the normalized calculus, spatial compositors and scalar comparisons for canonicalCoefficients m T; ringedRefinementClopen supplies OpenComparisons for these same operations. No witness is chosen in a definition.

Construct H as the actual scheme pullback of p.left and i.left, with its structure map to T through b. Lift k.left,r.left to s. properOpen_clopen_geometry makes s open and closed and gives sb=k, sq=r. Prove the pullback universal property in Over T explicitly by lifting the underlying scheme maps; uniqueness is pullback.hom_ext. This constructs the required Factorization.

Apply the clopen pullback coefficient compatibility to the three specified factors of t. At generic categories first identify the explicit properOpenMate constructor with the adjunction Hom equivalence applied to t(Rr_* M) followed by k_!(epsilon_r); specialize only the finished generic calculation. Apply refinement_coefficient_mate for p. Naturality of delta_k moves S(epsilon_r) to the left; the pullback coefficient identity replaces the resulting three factors. mateEquiv_counit for r turns lambda_r followed by S(epsilon_r) into r_B^*(chi_r) followed by epsilon_r,B. Naturality of t_B moves chi_r to the input. These equalities prove the required compatibility of the two p-transposes, so the Hom equivalence proves the desired square. All calculations are natural transformations and no chi or gamma is inverted.

Step 3: I checked the types of (*). Under restriction, k^*β=1, s^*π_s=1, and k^*δ, i^*δ are the λ identifications (open-tensor-normalization with g=id and A→B). The noncartesian case is handled through π_s. Steps 4–5: I recomputed (c), (g), (L) and (L'); all correct, and only δ, β, λ are inverted.
